subject: Science
text: A chemical reaction converts reactants into products. Evidence: colour change, gas evolution, precipitate, temperature change, smell change. Balanced equation obeys Law of Conservation of Mass - equal atoms on both sides. Types of reactions: Combination (2Mg+O2->2MgO, CaO+H2O->Ca(OH)2), Decomposition (thermal: CaCO3->CaO+CO2; electrolytic: 2H2O->2H2+O2; photolytic: 2AgBr->2Ag+Br2), Displacement (Fe+CuSO4->FeSO4+Cu), Double Displacement (Na2SO4+BaCl2->BaSO4+2NaCl with white precipitate). Oxidation = gain O2 or loss H2. Reduction = loss O2 or gain H2. OIL RIG mnemonic. CuO+H2->Cu+H2O: CuO reduced, H2 oxidised. Exothermic: combustion, neutralisation, respiration. Endothermic: photosynthesis, decomposition of CaCO3.

subject: Science
text: Corrosion: iron rusts via 4Fe+3O2+xH2O->2Fe2O3.xH2O. Needs both O2 and water. Salt water accelerates rusting. Prevention: painting, oiling, galvanisation (zinc coating - sacrificial), electroplating, alloying (stainless steel Fe+C+Cr+Ni). Silver tarnishes: 2Ag+H2S->Ag2S. Copper turns green: basic copper carbonate. Rancidity: oxidation of unsaturated fats/oils causing bad smell. Prevention: antioxidants (BHA, BHT, Vitamin E), vacuum/airtight packaging, refrigeration, nitrogen flushing in chips packets. Corrosion affects metals; rancidity affects food fats.

subject: Science
text: Acids produce H+ ions in water. Properties: sour taste, turn blue litmus red, pH below 7, react with metals releasing H2 gas. Strong acids (fully ionise): HCl, H2SO4, HNO3. Weak acids: CH3COOH (acetic acid in vinegar), H2CO3 (carbonic acid in soft drinks), citric acid (lemons). Acid + metal -> salt + H2. Acid + carbonate -> salt + H2O + CO2. CO2 test: lime water turns milky (Ca(OH)2+CO2->CaCO3+H2O). Bases produce OH- ions. Properties: bitter taste, soapy feel, turn red litmus blue, pH above 7. Alkalis = water-soluble bases. All alkalis are bases but not all bases are alkalis (CuO is base, insoluble in water).

subject: Science
text: pH scale 0-14: 7=neutral, below 7=acidic (lower=stronger), above 7=basic (higher=stronger). pH values: gastric juice 1-2, lemon 2-3, vinegar 3, milk 6.5, blood 7.35-7.45, baking soda 9, bleach 13. Tooth decay begins pH below 5.5. Acid rain pH below 5.6. Aquatic life needs pH 7-8.5. Indicators: Litmus (red in acid, blue in base), Phenolphthalein (colourless in acid, pink in base), Methyl orange (red in acid, yellow in base), Turmeric (yellow in acid/neutral, red in strong base). Neutralisation: acid+base->salt+water (exothermic). HCl+NaOH->NaCl+H2O. Applications: antacids Mg(OH)2/Al(OH)3 neutralise stomach HCl; lime neutralises acidic soil; baking soda treats bee stings (acidic); vinegar treats wasp stings (alkaline).

subject: Science
text: Important salts: NaCl (common salt) - food, NaOH manufacture, HCl, Na2CO3. NaHCO3 (baking soda) - baking (2NaHCO3->Na2CO3+H2O+CO2 on heating releases CO2 making bread rise), antacid, fire extinguisher. Na2CO3.10H2O (washing soda) - water softening by removing Ca2+/Mg2+, glass/soap manufacture. Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime) - whitewashing, treating acidic soil. CaOCl2 (bleaching powder, from Ca(OH)2+Cl2) - water treatment, bleaching cotton. Plaster of Paris CaSO4.0.5H2O - bone casts, statues (made by heating gypsum CaSO4.2H2O to 100-120 degrees). Water of crystallisation: CuSO4.5H2O (blue vitriol, blue->white when heated), FeSO4.7H2O (green vitriol), Na2CO3.10H2O. Chlor-alkali process electrolysis of brine gives Cl2 (anode), H2 (cathode), NaOH solution.

subject: Science
text: Physical properties of metals: lustrous, malleable (gold most malleable), ductile (gold most ductile, copper used for wires), sonorous, good conductors of heat and electricity (silver>copper>gold>aluminium), high density, high melting points. Exceptions: mercury liquid at room temp, Na/K soft and cut with knife, Li/Na/K less dense than water, gallium melts in hand. Non-metals: dull (except iodine/graphite), brittle, poor conductors (except graphite which is used in electrodes), low density, low melting points (except diamond). States: solid (S, P, C, I2), liquid (Br2), gas (O2, N2, H2, Cl2, noble gases). Activity series decreasing: K>Na>Ca>Mg>Al>Zn>Fe>Ni>Sn>Pb>H>Cu>Hg>Ag>Au>Pt. Stored in kerosene: K, Na, Ca (react vigorously with air/water).

subject: Science
text: Chemical properties of metals with oxygen: 4Na+O2->2Na2O, 2Mg+O2->2MgO (brilliant white), 2Cu+O2->2CuO (black), 3Fe+2O2->Fe3O4 (burns in pure O2 not air). Metal oxides are basic. With water: 2Na+2H2O->2NaOH+H2 (vigorous, room temp), Ca+2H2O->Ca(OH)2+H2 (moderate), Mg+H2O(steam)->MgO+H2, 3Fe+4H2O(steam)->Fe3O4+4H2, Cu/Ag/Au no reaction. With dilute acids: Zn+H2SO4->ZnSO4+H2, Fe+2HCl->FeCl2+H2. Metals below H in activity series (Cu,Hg,Ag,Au) do not react with dilute acids. Ionic bonding: Na(2,8,1) loses electron->Na+; Cl(2,8,7) gains electron->Cl-; electrostatic attraction forms NaCl. Properties of ionic compounds: crystalline solid, high melting point, hard and brittle, conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution (mobile ions), not in solid state (fixed ions).

subject: Science
text: Metal extraction from ores: Ore = mineral from which metal can be profitably extracted. Gangue = waste material. Low reactivity (Ag, Au): found free in nature. Medium reactivity (Fe, Zn, Pb, Sn): reduction with carbon. ZnO+C->Zn+CO. Fe2O3+3CO->2Fe+3CO2 in blast furnace. High reactivity (Na, Mg, Al, Ca, K): electrolytic reduction (carbon cannot reduce them). Al2O3 dissolved in molten cryolite, electrolysis produces Al at cathode. Thermite reaction: Fe2O3+2Al->Al2O3+2Fe+tremendous heat. Used for welding railway tracks. Electrolytic refining of copper: impure Cu (anode), pure Cu (cathode), CuSO4 solution (electrolyte). Cu dissolves from anode, deposits at cathode. Precious metals Ag/Au/Pt collect as anode mud. Alloys: Brass (Cu+Zn), Bronze (Cu+Sn), Solder (Pb+Sn, low melting for soldering), Stainless steel (Fe+C+Cr+Ni, rust-resistant), Duralumin (Al+Cu+Mg+Mn, aircraft).

subject: Science
text: Photosynthesis equation: 6CO2+6H2O+light energy->C6H12O6+6O2. Site: chloroplasts containing chlorophyll. Raw materials: CO2 enters via stomata; H2O absorbed by roots, transported via xylem. Products: glucose (stored as starch) and O2 released through stomata. Two stages: Light reaction in thylakoid membranes (grana) - absorbs light, splits water (photolysis), releases O2, produces ATP and NADPH. Dark reaction/Calvin cycle in stroma - CO2 fixed into glucose using ATP and NADPH, no direct light needed. Limiting factors: light intensity, CO2 concentration, temperature, water availability. Respiration: Aerobic: C6H12O6+6O2->6CO2+6H2O+38ATP. Stages: Glycolysis (cytoplasm, glucose->2 pyruvate, 2ATP), Krebs cycle (mitochondria matrix, pyruvate->CO2+NADH), ETC (inner mitochondrial membrane, most ATP). Anaerobic in yeast: glucose->2ethanol+2CO2+2ATP. Fermentation used in bread making (CO2 raises dough) and alcohol production. In muscle cells: glucose->2lactic acid+2ATP. Lactic acid causes muscle cramps; liver oxidises it when O2 available.

subject: Science
text: Human digestion complete pathway: Mouth: salivary amylase (ptyalin) converts starch to maltose at pH 6.8; teeth provide mechanical digestion; tongue forms bolus. Oesophagus: peristalsis (wave-like muscle contractions) moves bolus; epiglottis prevents food entering trachea. Stomach: gastric glands secrete HCl (pH 1-2, kills bacteria, activates pepsinogen->pepsin), pepsin (digests proteins to peptides), mucus (protects stomach lining), intrinsic factor (B12 absorption). Chyme forms. Small intestine (6-7m): duodenum receives bile from liver via bile duct (emulsifies fats, neutralises acid chyme) and pancreatic juice (amylase digests starch, lipase digests fats, trypsin/chymotrypsin digest proteins). Intestinal juice (maltase, sucrase, lactase, peptidases) completes digestion. Villi and microvilli increase surface area 600x for absorption. Glucose and amino acids absorbed into blood capillaries. Fatty acids and glycerol absorbed into lacteals (lymph). Large intestine: water and mineral absorption; bacteria synthesise Vitamin K and B12; faeces formed and stored in rectum until egestion.

subject: Science
text: Circulatory system: Double circulation - blood passes through heart twice per cycle. Pulmonary circuit: right ventricle->pulmonary artery->lungs (oxygenation)->pulmonary vein->left atrium. Systemic circuit: left ventricle->aorta->body tissues->vena cava->right atrium. Heart anatomy: 4 chambers (right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle). Valves: tricuspid (right AV), bicuspid/mitral (left AV), pulmonary semilunar (RV outlet), aortic semilunar (LV outlet). Left ventricle has thickest walls - pumps blood to entire body. Blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg (systolic/diastolic). Blood components: Plasma 55% (water, proteins, glucose, hormones, urea), RBC (haemoglobin carries O2, biconcave, no nucleus, 5 million/mm3, 120 day life), WBC (fight infection, produce antibodies, 5000-10000/mm3), Platelets (clotting via fibrinogen->fibrin). Lymph: tissue fluid entering lymph capillaries; transports fats from intestine; part of immune system. Excretion: Kidneys filter blood via 1 million nephrons each. Nephron function: glomerular filtration (high pressure filtration, blood cells and large proteins stay) -> tubular reabsorption (all glucose, most water, some salts reabsorbed) -> tubular secretion (H+, K+, drugs secreted) -> urine (urea, creatinine, excess salts, water). Urine pathway: collecting duct->renal pelvis->ureter->urinary bladder->urethra. Other excretory organs: Lungs (CO2, water vapour), Skin (sweat, water, salts), Liver (converts NH3 to urea, excretes bile pigments). Dialysis: artificial kidney for renal failure patients.

subject: Science
text: Neuron structure: cell body (soma) with nucleus, dendrites (receive signals), axon (transmits signals away, covered by myelin sheath which speeds conduction), axon terminals (synaptic knobs). Neuron types: Sensory/afferent (receptors to CNS), Motor/efferent (CNS to effectors), Relay/interneuron (within CNS). Nerve impulse: resting membrane negative inside (polarised). Stimulus causes Na+ influx -> depolarisation (inside becomes positive) -> signal propagates along axon -> K+ efflux causes repolarisation. Synapse: 20-40nm gap between neurons. Process: action potential arrives at presynaptic terminal -> neurotransmitter vesicles fuse with membrane -> neurotransmitters (acetylcholine, dopamine) released into cleft -> bind to receptors on postsynaptic neuron -> new impulse generated. Reflex arc: Stimulus->receptor->sensory neuron->spinal cord relay neuron->motor neuron->effector->response. Response occurs before brain processes (faster). Brain informed simultaneously via ascending pathways. Examples of reflexes: withdrawing hand from hot object, knee-jerk, blinking, pupillary response, sneezing.

subject: Science
text: Human brain regions: Forebrain - Cerebrum (two hemispheres connected by corpus callosum): sensory areas, motor areas, association areas for thinking/memory/intelligence/language/personality/consciousness. Thalamus: relay station for sensory information. Hypothalamus: regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst, sleep, emotions, controls pituitary gland. Midbrain: visual and auditory reflexes, regulates eye movement. Hindbrain - Cerebellum: balance, posture, coordination of voluntary movements (damaged = ataxia). Pons: breathing rhythm, relay between cerebrum and cerebellum. Medulla oblongata: controls vital involuntary functions (heartbeat, breathing, blood pressure, swallowing, vomiting), connects brain to spinal cord. Brain protected by skull, meninges (3 layers), cerebrospinal fluid. Plant hormones: Auxins (IAA, produced at shoot apex): cell elongation, phototropism (bends towards light as auxin moves to shaded side), geotropism (roots opposite to shoots), apical dominance. Gibberellins: stem elongation, seed germination, parthenocarpy (fruit without fertilisation). Cytokinins: cell division, delays leaf senescence. Abscisic acid (ABA): inhibitor, closes stomata in drought, seed dormancy, promotes leaf/fruit abscission. Ethylene (gas): fruit ripening, commercially used for bananas, promotes senescence.

subject: Science
text: Human endocrine system complete: Pituitary (master gland, base of brain): GH (growth hormone; excess=gigantism; deficiency=dwarfism), TSH (stimulates thyroid), FSH and LH (reproductive cycle), ADH (water reabsorption in kidneys; deficiency=diabetes insipidus), Prolactin (milk production), Oxytocin (uterine contractions, milk release). Thyroid (neck, butterfly-shaped): Thyroxine/T4 and T3 regulate basal metabolic rate; require iodine. Deficiency: goitre (enlarged thyroid), hypothyroidism (low BMR, fatigue, weight gain); in children cretinism (stunted physical and mental growth). Hyperthyroidism (Graves disease): high BMR, weight loss, bulging eyes. Parathyroid: PTH regulates Ca2+ and phosphate levels. Pancreas - Islets of Langerhans: Beta cells secrete insulin (lowers blood glucose by stimulating cellular uptake and glycogen synthesis in liver). Alpha cells secrete glucagon (raises blood glucose by stimulating glycogen breakdown in liver). Diabetes mellitus: Type 1 (no insulin produced, juvenile onset), Type 2 (insulin resistance, adult onset). Adrenal cortex: cortisol (stress response, glucose regulation), aldosterone (Na+/K+ balance, blood pressure). Adrenal medulla: adrenaline (epinephrine) - fight or flight: increases heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure, blood glucose; dilates pupils; increases blood flow to muscles. Gonads: Testes - testosterone (spermatogenesis, secondary male sexual characteristics: voice deepening, beard, muscle development). Ovaries - oestrogen (follicle development, secondary female characteristics: breast development, hip widening), progesterone (prepares uterine lining for implantation, maintains pregnancy).

subject: Science
text: Asexual reproduction: single parent, no gametes, genetically identical offspring (clones). Types: Binary fission - organism divides into two equal daughter cells. Amoeba divides in any plane, bacteria in specific plane, Leishmania along length of body. Multiple fission - Plasmodium (malarial parasite) divides into many merozoites in human liver/blood cells simultaneously. Fragmentation - body breaks into pieces each developing into new organism: Spirogyra (filamentous alga), Planaria (flatworm). Regeneration - ability to regrow from a piece: Planaria can regenerate from tiny fragment, Hydra. Budding - small outgrowth forms on parent, detaches and grows: Hydra (from body wall), yeast (from cell surface - common in fermentation). Spore formation - parent produces hundreds of microscopic spores with thick protective walls: Rhizopus (black bread mould, black sporangia release spores). Also in ferns and mosses. Vegetative propagation - natural: runners/stolons (grass, strawberry), rhizomes (ginger, turmeric), bulbs (onion, garlic), corms (colocasia), tubers (potato - eyes are axillary buds), leaves (Bryophyllum - adventitious buds on leaf margins). Artificial: cutting (rose, sugarcane), layering (jasmine), grafting (mango, apple), tissue culture/micropropagation. Advantages: maintains desired characteristics, faster than seed method.

subject: Science
text: Sexual reproduction in plants: Flower is reproductive organ. Male: Androecium = stamens (anther produces pollen grains with male gametes + filament). Female: Gynoecium/Pistil = stigma (receives pollen) + style + ovary (contains ovules with female gametes). Pollination: Self-pollination (same flower/plant), Cross-pollination (different plant of same species - produces more genetic variation). Agents: Wind (light pollen, feathery stigma), Insects (fragrant flowers, nectar, bright colours, sticky pollen), Water, Birds, Bats. Fertilisation: pollen grain germinates on stigma, pollen tube grows through style to ovule, releases male gametes. Double fertilisation (unique to angiosperms): first male gamete (n) + egg cell (n) = zygote (2n) -> embryo. Second male gamete (n) + two polar nuclei (n+n) = triploid nucleus (3n) -> endosperm (food for embryo). Post-fertilisation: Ovule->seed. Ovary wall (pericarp)->fruit wall. Rest of flower (sepals, petals, stamens) wither. Seed = embryo + food + testa (seed coat) + tegmen.

subject: Science
text: Human reproduction: Male system: Testes (in scrotal sac, 2-3 degrees C below body temp for sperm production) produce sperm and testosterone. Seminiferous tubules: site of spermatogenesis. Interstitial cells (Leydig cells): testosterone production. Epididymis: sperm maturation and storage. Vas deferens: carries sperm. Seminal vesicles: add fructose (energy for sperm). Prostate gland: adds alkaline fluid (neutralises vaginal acidity). Cowper glands (bulbourethral): lubrication. Urethra and penis: delivery. Semen = sperm + glandular secretions. Sperm structure: head (nucleus with 23 chromosomes + acrosome with hydrolytic enzymes to penetrate egg), middle piece (mitochondria for ATP/energy), tail (flagellum for motility). Female system: Ovaries (produce eggs by oogenesis - one per month; secrete oestrogen and progesterone). Graafian follicle matures monthly. Fallopian tubes: fimbriae sweep egg in; site of fertilisation; cilia and peristalsis move egg towards uterus. Uterus: implantation site; endometrium thickens under oestrogen/progesterone influence; site of foetal development. Cervix: neck of uterus. Vagina: birth canal, receives semen. Menstrual cycle 28 days: Days 1-5 menstruation (endometrium shed as progesterone drops - no fertilisation). Days 6-13 follicular phase (FSH stimulates follicle, oestrogen thickens endometrium). Day 14 ovulation (LH surge from pituitary, Graafian follicle ruptures, egg released - viable 24 hrs; sperm survive 2-3 days). Days 15-28 luteal phase (corpus luteum forms, secretes progesterone, endometrium thickens further). If no fertilisation: corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone drops -> menstruation. Fertilisation in fallopian tube -> zygote -> cleavage -> morula -> blastocyst -> implants in endometrium day 6-10. Placenta: exchange organ (nutrients, O2, antibodies to foetus; CO2, waste from foetus). Pregnancy 38-40 weeks.

subject: Science
text: Laws of reflection: angle of incidence (i) = angle of reflection (r). Both rays and normal are in same plane. Regular reflection: smooth surfaces (mirrors). Diffuse reflection: rough surfaces. Terms: Pole (P) = geometric centre of mirror. Principal axis = line through P and centre of curvature C. Centre of curvature (C) = centre of sphere. Radius of curvature (R). Focus (F) = point where parallel rays meet (concave) or appear to diverge from (convex) after reflection. Focal length f = R/2. Concave mirror: real focus in front. Convex mirror: virtual focus behind. Plane mirror image: virtual, erect, same size, laterally inverted, same distance behind mirror. Image formation in concave mirror: Object at infinity->image at F (real, inverted, point). Beyond C->between C and F (real, inverted, diminished). At C->at C (real, inverted, same size). Between C and F->beyond C (real, inverted, magnified). At F->at infinity (no image, parallel beam - used in torches). Between F and P->behind mirror (virtual, erect, magnified - used in shaving/makeup mirror). Convex mirror always: virtual, erect, diminished. Uses: rear-view mirrors, security mirrors, street corner mirrors (wider field of view).

subject: Science
text: Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. New Cartesian sign convention: all distances measured from pole P. Distances in direction of incident light = positive. Distances opposite to incident light = negative. Object always in front, so u always negative. Real image in front of mirror: v negative. Virtual image behind: v positive. Concave mirror: f negative. Convex mirror: f positive. Magnification m = -v/u = h2/h1. Negative m: real inverted image. Positive m: virtual erect image. |m|>1: magnified. |m|<1: diminished. |m|=1: same size. Refraction: bending of light when passing from one transparent medium to another due to change in speed. Speed in vacuum c = 3x10^8 m/s. In denser medium speed decreases. Rarer to denser: bends towards normal (angle of refraction < angle of incidence). Denser to rarer: bends away from normal. Snell law: n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r). Refractive index n = c/v = sin(i)/sin(r). Values: water 1.33, glass 1.5, diamond 2.42. Phenomena due to refraction: apparent depth, twinkling of stars (atmospheric refraction), rainbow, mirage. Total internal reflection: when angle exceeds critical angle in denser medium, all light reflects internally. Applications: optical fibres, endoscopes, diamond sparkle.

subject: Science
text: Lenses: Convex (converging) - thicker at centre, converges parallel rays at real focus F. Concave (diverging) - thicker at edges, appears to diverge parallel rays from virtual focus F. Lens formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f. Sign convention: u always negative. Convex: positive f. Concave: negative f. Real image (other side): v positive. Virtual (same side as object): v negative. Magnification m = v/u (no negative sign, unlike mirror). Image formation by convex lens: Object beyond 2F->between F and 2F on other side (real, inverted, diminished - camera, eye). At 2F->at 2F other side (real, inverted, same size). Between F and 2F->beyond 2F other side (real, inverted, magnified - projector, slide projector). At F->parallel beam (no image). Between F and O->same side as object (virtual, erect, magnified - magnifying glass, reading glass). Concave lens always: virtual, erect, diminished on same side as object. Power P = 1/f (in metres), unit dioptre (D). Convex: positive P. Concave: negative P. Combination: P_total = P1+P2. Eye defects: Myopia (short-sight) - image forms in front of retina, distant objects blurred, corrected by concave lens. Hypermetropia (long-sight) - image behind retina, near objects blurred, corrected by convex lens. Presbyopia: loss of accommodation with age, bifocal lenses. Astigmatism: unequal corneal curvature, cylindrical lenses.

subject: Science
text: Electric charge Q in coulombs (C). Current I = Q/t in amperes (A). 1 ampere = 1 coulomb per second. Conventional current: positive to negative. Electron flow: negative to positive (opposite). Ammeter: measures current, connected in series, very low resistance. Potential difference V = W/Q in volts (V). Voltmeter: measures PD, connected in parallel, very high resistance. Ohm law: V = IR at constant temperature. R = V/I in ohms (omega). Ohm law graph: straight line through origin (V vs I). Non-ohmic devices: tungsten filament bulb (R increases with temperature), semiconductor diode (one-directional), LED. Resistance factors: R = rhoL/A where rho = resistivity (material property, ohm-metre), L = length (R proportional to L), A = cross-sectional area (R inversely proportional to A), temperature (metals: R increases with temp; semiconductors: R decreases with temp). Resistivity: silver 1.6e-8, copper 1.7e-8, nichrome 100e-8 ohm-m. Nichrome used in heating elements (high resistivity, high melting point).

subject: Science
text: Series circuit: Components connected end-to-end, single path for current. Current same through all resistors: I = I1 = I2 = I3. Voltage divides: V = V1+V2+V3. Equivalent resistance: R_s = R1+R2+R3 (always greater than any individual). If one component fails, entire circuit breaks. Parallel circuit: Components between same two points, multiple current paths. Voltage same across all: V = V1 = V2 = V3. Current divides: I = I1+I2+I3. Equivalent resistance: 1/R_p = 1/R1+1/R2+1/R3 (always less than smallest individual). If one fails, others continue. Household wiring: always parallel (each appliance gets full 220-240V, independent switching). Example: R1=6 ohm, R2=3 ohm in parallel: 1/Rp=1/6+1/3=1/2, Rp=2 ohm. In series: Rs=6+3=9 ohm. Power P = VI = I^2 R = V^2/R in watts (W). Energy E = Pt = I^2 Rt in joules or kWh. 1 kWh = 3.6x10^6 J = 1 unit of electricity on bill. Joule heating H = I^2 Rt. Applications: heater, iron, toaster, geyser, incandescent bulb (tungsten filament, mp=3380 degrees C). Fuse: thin Sn-Pb alloy wire, low melting point, placed in series in live wire, melts on overload. MCB: modern fuse that can be reset. Three-pin plug: earth (green, largest pin, safety), live (brown/red), neutral (blue/black).

subject: Science
text: Oersted discovery 1820: current in conductor produces magnetic field around it (demonstrated by deflecting compass needle). Right-hand thumb rule: if right thumb points in direction of current, curled fingers show direction of magnetic field circles. Field is stronger closer to wire and increases with current. Magnetic field of circular loop: at centre, field lines straight and uniform, perpendicular to plane of loop. Centre behaves like a magnet. Solenoid: cylindrical coil of insulated wire. Field inside is uniform and parallel to axis, behaves exactly like bar magnet with well-defined N and S poles. Field strength increases with: number of turns N, current I, soft iron core (electromagnet). Electromagnet: solenoid+soft iron core. Loses magnetism when current stops (unlike permanent magnet). Uses: cranes, doorbells, loudspeakers, relays, MRI machines, particle accelerators. Force on current-carrying conductor: F = BIL sin(theta). Maximum when current perpendicular to field (theta=90), zero when parallel. Fleming left-hand rule: stretch thumb, index finger, middle finger of left hand mutually perpendicular. Index finger = direction of B field. Middle finger = direction of conventional current I. Thumb = direction of force/thrust F.

subject: Science
text: Electric motor: converts electrical energy to mechanical/rotational energy. Principle: current in magnetic field experiences force. Components: rectangular armature coil of insulated copper wire wound on soft iron core (increases flux), strong permanent magnets, split-ring commutator (two half rings), carbon brushes. Working: current in AB side experiences upward force, CD downward force -> coil rotates. At 180 degrees, commutator reverses current direction maintaining rotation in same direction. Split-ring commutator is essential for DC motor operation. Uses: fans, pumps, mixers, washing machines, electric vehicles. Electromagnetic induction: changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces EMF and current. Faraday laws: (1) EMF is induced whenever magnetic flux through circuit changes. (2) Magnitude of induced EMF is proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux. Lenz law: direction of induced current opposes the cause producing it (conservation of energy). Fleming right-hand rule: for generators. Thumb=motion of conductor (velocity), index finger=B field direction, middle finger=induced current direction. AC generator: armature coil rotates in magnetic field; two complete slip rings allow continuous rotation; produces alternating EMF. Frequency = rotation frequency (50 Hz in India = 50 cycles/second). Transformer: changes AC voltage by mutual electromagnetic induction. Step-up: Ns>Np, increases V, decreases I. Step-down: Ns<Np, decreases V, increases I. Equation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = Ip/Is. Ideal: power input = power output (VpIp = VsIs). Power transmission: generating stations step up to 400kV for long distance (reduces I^2R losses); substations step down to 240V for homes.
